'''Wang Yifang''' ({{zh|s=王贻芳}}; born February 1963) is a Chinese particle and accelerator [[physicist]]. He is director of the [[Institute of High Energy Physics]] (IHEP) of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in [[Beijing]] and known for contributions to [[neutrino]] physics, in particular his leading role (with [[Kam-Biu Luk]]) at [[Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment]] to determine the last unknown neutrino mixing angle {{mvar|θ}}{{sub|13}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Wang Yifang----Institute of High Energy Physics|url = http://english.ihep.cas.cn/pe/staff/200909/t20090902_35275.html|website = english.ihep.cas.cn|access-date = 2016-02-03|archive-date = 2016-03-04|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160304041119/http://english.ihep.cas.cn/pe/staff/200909/t20090902_35275.html|url-status = dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
After earning his bachelor's degree in physics at  [[Nanjing University]] in 1984, he worked with [[Samuel CC Ting]] on the [[L3 experiment]] located at the [[Large Electron–Positron Collider|Large Electron-Positron Collider]] (LEP) of [[CERN]]. Wang studied at the [[University of Florence]], obtaining his PhD in Physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WANG Yifang----Institute of High Energy Physics |url=http://english.ihep.cas.cn/doc/1747.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027064405/http://english.ihep.cas.cn/doc/1747.html |archive-date=2021-10-27 |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=english.ihep.cas.cn}}</ref> He would then go on to work for the Laboratory for Nuclear Science located at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and later at [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=INSPIRE: Yifang Wang—author profile|url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/984106|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-18|website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> He later joined the Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP) in China as a researcher in 2001, eventually becoming the director in 2011.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Prize Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|access-date=2021-01-18|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 2014 [[Panofsky Prize]] (shared with [[Kam-Biu Luk]])<ref name=":0" /> 
* 2015 Member of [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]
* 2016 [[Fundamental Physics Prize|Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]], with [[Kam-Biu Luk]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Breakthrough Prize|url = https://breakthroughprize.org/News/29|website = breakthroughprize.org|access-date = 2016-02-03}}</ref> 
* 2016 Member of [[The World Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://english.cas.cn/newsroom/news/201611/t20161117_170678.shtml|title=Nine CAS Scientists Elected TWAS Fellows|date=2016-11-17|publisher=[[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=2019-05-05}}</ref>
* 2016 and 2020 [[Asian Scientist 100]], ''[[Asian Scientist]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>
* 2019 [[Future Science Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wang Yifang wins 2019 Future Science Prize----Institute of High Energy Physics|url=http://english.ihep.cas.cn/doc/3744.html|access-date=2020-12-24|website=english.ihep.cas.cn|archive-date=2020-05-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200517024702/http://english.ihep.cas.cn/doc/3744.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2022 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2022|title=Fellows nominated in 2022|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2022-10-19}}</ref>
* 2024 Foreign associates of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite news |author1=Ni Sijie ({{lang|zh|倪思洁}}) |url=https://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2024/5/522012.shtm |script-title=zh:王贻芳当选为美国国家科学院外籍院士 |work=sciencenet.cn |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=4 May 2024 |language=zh}}</ref>
* 2025 Foreign Member of the [[Royal Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>

Since 2014 Wang has been Director of the [[Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory]] (JUNO) in Southern China leading the experiment in an effect to determine the neutrino mass hierarchy with neutrinos from nuclear reactors.<ref name=":0" />
